campaign_name: Initiative 26-02: Reduce state personal income tax rate from 5% to 4% (2028)
purpose: Cut personal income tax rate from 5.00% to 4.00% over three years (4.67% 2029, 4.33% 2030, 4.00% from 2031)
sponsor: Brian Shortsleeve (listed proponent on AG filing). The 2026 version was backed by Taxpayers for an Affordable Massachusetts (spokesperson Chris Keohan), which hinted at a 2028 retry; whether that committee is running 26-02 is unknown
signatures_required: 74,574 (first round); additional round if Legislature does not act (2026-cycle figure was 12,429; 2028 figure unknown)
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local election officials; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth
budget_or_spend: unknown. Shortsleeve paid Hubschman's SignatureDrive tens of thousands of dollars as a 2026 candidate (Boston Globe)
evidence_note: The AG certified it (Foley Hoag, Sept 2026). The 2026 version of this tax cut collected signatures but the SJC removed it from the ballot in June 2026, and Shortsleeve vowed to restart the effort. No source found showing that 2028 collection is underway or that a firm has been hired. Hubschman also filed a near-identical version (26-13), which was not certified. This is the most likely well-funded 2028 drive.

purpose: 10 certified proposed laws: collective bargaining for state employees (26-05) and legislative employees (26-06); 1% internet ad tax for social-media safety (26-09); clean-energy tax credit (26-10); eliminate legislative stipends (26-11); end state gas tax (26-12); 2.5% per-parcel property tax cap, versions A and B (26-14, 26-15); larceny over $250 a felony (26-16); sales tax cut from 6.25% to 5% (26-17)
sponsor: Harold Hubschman (filer). As of Sept 22, 2026, the Boston Globe reported that no group had taken up any of these proposals
circulation_firm: SignatureDrive.com (Hubschman's firm) would be the natural vendor, but it is not confirmed collecting on these
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local election officials; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth
budget_or_spend: No 2028 spend found. SignatureDrive.com has taken in at least $4.6M since the start of 2025 from ballot committees and candidates (Boston Globe)
website: https://www.signaturedrive.com/ (named in the Boston Globe; not fetched)
evidence_note: A signature-firm owner filed these as products he can pitch to funders. 26-07 and 26-13 were filed but not certified. Any of the 10 could become a paid drive if a funder buys in before Nov 18. These are prime prospects for a petition-management pitch: the measures are certified but have no client yet.

campaign_name: Initiative 26-08: Regulating construction, expansion and operation of data centers (2028)
purpose: Require local voter approval and other conditions (electricity supply contracts, financial guarantees) for data center permits
circulation_firm: unknown. Boston.com reports Fleming is tied to JEF Associates, which provides certified signatures and ballot-initiative services; not confirmed as the vendor for this drive
signatures_required: 74,574 (first round); about 12,500 more if the Legislature does not act
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local election officials; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth
evidence_note: Certified per Foley Hoag. Ballotpedia calls it the nation's second statewide data-center measure. There is no evidence of funding or paid circulation. Possible prospect: environmental or anti-data-center groups would be natural funders.

campaign_name: Initiatives 26-01 (non-ionizing radiation office) and 26-18 (lifetime license-revocation hardship waiver) (2028)
purpose: 26-01: create an Office of Research and Technology Optimization, a public radiation map and fee-based testing. 26-18: hardship license pathway for drivers with lifetime license revocations
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local election officials; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth
evidence_note: Both were filed by individuals and certified. No evidence of funding, a committee or paid circulators. Probably volunteer-only or dormant (inference). Low-probability prospects.

campaign_name: Referendum on Chapter 188 (H.5595) abortion law – Compassionate Care Coalition (2028)
purpose: Repeal (and suspend until the vote) the abortion law Gov. Healey signed Aug 10, 2026, which removes restrictions on abortions after 24 weeks
sponsor: Compassionate Care Coalition: Massachusetts Citizens for Life (president Myrna Maloney Flynn) and Massachusetts Family Action (Sam Miele, coalition chair)
signatures_required: 37,289 to place on the 2028 ballot; 49,719 to suspend the law until the vote
deadline: Oct 23, 2026 to local election officials (passed); Nov 6, 2026 to Secretary of the Commonwealth
decision_maker: Sam Miele (coalition chair, Massachusetts Family Action); Myrna Maloney Flynn (MCFL)
contact: unknown (no coalition website listed; parent orgs Massachusetts Citizens for Life and Massachusetts Family Action/Massachusetts Family Institute have their own sites)
evidence_note: Filed Sept 1, 2026. The fall circulation window to local clerks closed Oct 23, 2026, the day before this check, so it is marked completed for collection. The result (count submitted, whether it suspends the law, any emergency preamble from Healey) is unknown. No source states whether circulators were paid or volunteer. Next action: the Nov 6 filing with the Secretary of the Commonwealth.

purpose: Zoning reform to allow starter homes
circulation_firm: unknown (professional signature gathering confirmed; firm not named in the sources fetched)
budget_or_spend: More than $1.4M paid for signature gathering (Boston Globe, Sept 2026); about $1.3M professional signature gathering cited by State House News Service (Feb 2026)
evidence_note: The drive is finished and the measure is on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot as Question 7. It is the largest documented MA paid signature spend this cycle and a benchmark for pricing a 2028 statewide drive at roughly $1.3M to $1.4M.

campaign_name: Coalition for Healthy Democracy petition crews (The Outreach Team / Movement Builders)
purpose: Hourly-paid petition circulator crews for Massachusetts initiatives (2024–2026 cycles)
sponsor: Coalition for Healthy Democracy (per job ads)
pay_rate: Aug 26, 2025 Movement Builders ad (Amherst): $20/hr circulator, $22/hr team lead, plus bonuses and overtime. The Outreach Team (Boston): $21/hr circulator, $23/hr team lead, daily bonuses up to $170 (posting closed). Earlier ads: $19–21/hr, bonuses of $50–200/day
evidence_note: These are the only MA circulator pay rates found. The newest is from Aug 2025 (2026 cycle). No fall-2026 posting for 2028 petitions was found. These hourly rates are a useful benchmark against the per-signature model the Legislature is considering banning (Finegold bill).

campaign_name: An Act to Amend the Cannabis Legalization Act and the Maine Medical Use of Cannabis Act
purpose: Roll back or restrict Maine's adult-use and medical cannabis laws (described as an anti-cannabis/prohibitionist effort)
sponsor: unknown (Secretary of State's 'Proponent Information' page not fetched)
circulation_firm: unknown. Out-of-state paid circulators were reported
deadline: June 8, 2027 filing deadline (for a 2027 election); Feb 2, 2026 was the 2026 cutoff
pay_rate: $1 per signature (one circulator, in a recording reported Jan 2026)
contact: Maine Division of Elections 207-624-7650 (state office, for proponent records)
evidence_note: Approved for circulation Dec 8, 2025. In Jan 2026, Secretary Bellows testified that circulators were 'people for hire' shipped in from out of state. A Texas circulator said he was paid $1 per signature. The SOS page still lists it as current, with a June 8, 2027 deadline. Not verified whether signatures were filed for 2026 or whether paid collection continues in Oct 2026.

campaign_name: Resolve directing development of a publicly funded health care system for all Maine residents
purpose: Direct the Legislature to develop universal publicly funded health care
sponsor: Maine AllCare / HealthCare for All Maine (501(c)(4) arm)
circulation_firm: unknown (appears volunteer-driven; commenters describe themselves as canvassers)
contact: Maine AllCare, PO Box 190, Manchester, ME 04351; info@maineallcare.org
evidence_note: Approved for circulation Oct 24, 2025. A July 2, 2026 post describes an active campaign for the 2027 ballot. No evidence of paid circulators. Possible prospect for professional field help as the deadline approaches.

campaign_name: An Act to Designate School Sports Participation and Facilities by Sex ('Protect Girls Sports in Maine')
purpose: Limit school sports participation, and bathroom and locker room use, to sex at birth
sponsor: unknown (SOS page references a petition organization registration mentioning 'Morning in American II'; not confirmed as the applicant)
circulation_firm: unknown. Out-of-state circulators were a prominent factor in the signature review
deadline: Petitions submitted; filing deadline listed as May 3, 2027
signatures_collected: unknown (SOS first validated in March 2026, then found too few valid signatures after a legal challenge)
evidence_note: Signatures were submitted, and the review was in the courts as of May 2026. Collection appears finished. Because the issue date was Nov 3, 2025 and the window runs to May 3, 2027, a supplemental drive is possible but not verified.
